description: Every server → client message of protocol v0 (docs/protocol.md, "Server → client") as the bytes sent in one text frame: one compact JSON object, no whitespace, never a raw newline (HK-233). welcome is {type, protocol: 0, app: "PowerUp", version} (HK-234); status {type, status} with the fixed wire names (HK-230); transcript {type, entry: {id, kind, text, date}} with the id uppercase (uuidString) and the date as Unix seconds (HK-231); session {type, model, effort, permissionMode, controlMode, costUSD} plus tokens only when above zero and liveModel and sessionID only when present and not empty (HK-232); pong {type}; error {type, code, message}. Swift writes the members in a hash order that changes from launch to launch, so the table fixes the order shown (type first, then the order above, entry as id, kind, text, date, session's optional members as tokens, liveModel, sessionID), and writes strings and numbers exactly as JSONSerialization wrote them. Strings escape ", \, / (as \/), \b \f \n \r \t and the other C0 controls as lowercase \u00xx; DEL and all non-ASCII are raw. Integers are decimal; a Double is written as printf's %.17g would (17 significant digits, trailing zeros dropped, the exponent form d.dddde±XX below 1e-4 and from 1e17 on), so 0.0421 is 0.042099999999999999: not the shortest round-trip digits JSONEncoder writes (json::encoder). A message holding a non-finite number is no valid JSON and is never sent (expected null).
function: PowerUpProtocol.welcome(appVersion:), status(_:), transcript(_:), session(model:liveModel:effort:permissionMode:controlMode:sessionID:costUSD:tokens:), pong(), error(code:message:) then encode(_:) — input {type, ...fields}: the message type and the builder's arguments (costUSD a number, or the string "nan", "infinity" or "-0" for a Double JSON cannot spell or a reader may not keep; liveModel and sessionID a string or null), expected the frame payload's exact text, or null when encode refuses it
verifiedBy: DESIGN.md v1.7; docs/protocol.md spec v0; Tests/PowerUpTests/ProtocolFixtureTests.swift testServerMessageTable builds each CoreBridge.ServerMessage, encodes it through the bridge (CoreBridge.protocolEncode(_:)) and compares the text byte for byte. Rust: rust/powerup-core/tests/protocol.rs server_message_cases builds each protocol::message::ServerMessage, runs protocol::message::encode and compares the text byte for byte (the core writes the order the table shows).
capturedAgainst: Swift 5.9.2 Foundation and CryptoKit (Xcode 15.2) on macOS 27.2, PowerUp at 2d20afb

cases.reason: %.17g drops trailing zeros, so 123456.789 stays short.

cases.name: session cost 1e16 is plain digits
cases.reason: Under 17 digits before the point, %.17g writes plain digits.

cases.name: session cost 1e17 uses the exponent form
cases.reason: At 17 digits before the point, %.17g switches to the exponent form.

cases.name: session cost 0.0001 is plain digits
cases.reason: An exponent of -4 is still written plain.

cases.name: session cost 0.00001 uses the exponent form
cases.reason: Below 1e-4 the exponent form, with all 17 digits.

cases.reason: A negative cost is written as it is.

cases.reason: Negative zero is written -0.

cases.reason: encode returns nil for an object that is not valid JSON, so the message is never sent (HK-233).
